```{python}
import sys

from shared.glossary import glossary_popovers
from shared.components import (
    chart_card,
    method_and_sources,
    prev_next,
    related_studies,
    stat_tile,
    stat_tiles,
)
from shared.outputs import read_output
from shared.paths import CASE_STUDIES, REPO_URL, ROOT

STUDY = CASE_STUDIES / "02_crime_statistics"
sys.path.insert(0, str(STUDY / "analysis"))
import figures as F  # noqa: E402

rows, prov_rows, notes_rows = read_output(STUDY / "outputs" / "crime_offences.csv")
totals, prov_totals, notes_totals = read_output(STUDY / "outputs" / "crime_totals.csv")

FIRST, LAST = int(rows.year.min()), int(rows.year.max())
PROPERTY, BODY = "Against Property", "Against Human Body"
PENAL, VARIOUS = "Other Offences Against Penal Code", "Against Various Acts"
DRUGS, CUSTOMS = "Against Misuses of Drug Act", "Against Customs & Excise Act"
IMMIGRATION, LABOUR = "Against Immigration Act", "Against Labour Act"

t = totals.set_index(["handled_by", "year"])
r = rows.set_index(["handled_by", "offence", "year"])


def num(v):
    return f"{v:,.0f}"


def pct(v, d=0):
    return f"{v:.{d}f}%"


def rise(v, d=1):
    """Size of a rise or fall for prose ("rose 9.3%"), where the verb carries the sign."""
    return f"{abs(v):.{d}f}%"


def signed(v, d=1):
    return f"{v:+.{d}f}%".replace("-", "−")


def change(handled_by, offence):
    a, b = r.loc[(handled_by, offence, FIRST), "cases"], r.loc[(handled_by, offence, LAST), "cases"]
    return (b / a - 1) * 100


def share(handled_by, offence, year=LAST):
    """Share of cases from the counts, not the rounded share column, to avoid double rounding."""
    return r.loc[(handled_by, offence, year), "cases"] / t.loc[(handled_by, year), "cases"] * 100


def police(offence, col, year=LAST):
    return r.loc[("police", offence, year), col]


def other(offence, col, year=LAST):
    return r.loc[("other agencies", offence, year), col]


cases_first, cases_last = t.loc[("police", FIRST), "cases"], t.loc[("police", LAST), "cases"]
cases_change = (cases_last / cases_first - 1) * 100
prop_share_first = share("police", PROPERTY, FIRST)
prop_share_last = share("police", PROPERTY)
penal_share = share("police", PROPERTY) + share("police", PENAL)
solved_first = t.loc[("police", FIRST), "solved"] / cases_first * 100
solved_last = t.loc[("police", LAST), "solved"] / cases_last * 100
prop_extra = police(PROPERTY, "cases") - police(PROPERTY, "cases", FIRST)
police_extra = cases_last - cases_first
other_first, other_last = t.loc[("other agencies", FIRST), "cases"], t.loc[("other agencies", LAST), "cases"]
drug_share_last = share("other agencies", DRUGS)
customs_share_last = share("other agencies", CUSTOMS)
```

::: {.study-intro}
This case study looks at the **crime statistics published by the Royal Brunei Police Force
for 2012 and 2013**: how many cases were recorded, what kinds of offences they were, how many
were solved and how many people were arrested. These are the only two years available on
data.gov.bn, so this is **a snapshot from over a decade ago, not a picture of crime today**. It
shows what was recorded, not why.

It asks two questions, answered in the conclusion:

1. **What kinds of offences made up police cases, and how many were solved?**
2. **What changed from 2012 to 2013?**
:::

```{python}
stat_tiles(
    stat_tile(f"Police cases, {LAST}", num(cases_last), signed(cases_change), f"vs {FIRST} ({num(cases_first)})"),
    stat_tile(f"Against property, {LAST}", pct(prop_share_last), "", f"of police cases ({FIRST}: {pct(prop_share_first)})"),
    stat_tile(f"Police cases solved, {LAST}", pct(solved_last), "", f"{FIRST}: {pct(solved_first)}"),
)
```

```{python}
fig, table = F.police_cases(rows)
chart_card(
    fig,
    title="Nearly two in three police cases were offences against property",
    subtitle=f"Cases handled by police, by type of offence · {FIRST} and {LAST}",
    alt=(
        f"Bar chart of police cases by type of offence. Offences against property are the "
        f"largest group in both years ({num(police(PROPERTY, 'cases', FIRST))} in {FIRST}, "
        f"{num(police(PROPERTY, 'cases'))} in {LAST}), followed by other Penal Code offences, "
        f"offences against the human body and various Acts."
    ),
    provenance=prov_rows,
    table=table,
    height=380,
)
```

## Cases handled by police, 2012–2013

The police table groups cases into four types. Offences against property were the largest:
`{python} pct(prop_share_first)` of police cases in `{python} FIRST` and
`{python} pct(prop_share_last)` in `{python} LAST`. Together with other Penal Code offences,
they made up `{python} pct(penal_share)` of police cases in `{python} LAST`. Offences against
the human body were about one in ten (`{python} num(police(BODY, "cases"))` cases in
`{python} LAST`).

### Cases solved

The share of cases [solved]{.term term="solved-case"} differed widely by type of offence. In `{python} LAST`, about
`{python} pct(police(BODY, "solved_pct"))` of offences against the human body were recorded as
solved, against `{python} pct(police(PROPERTY, "solved_pct"))` of offences against property.
Because property offences were the largest group, the share solved across all police cases
was `{python} pct(solved_last)`.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="What “solved” means here"}
The source counts cases as **solved** but doesn't define the term or say when it was counted,
for example whether a case reported in December and solved the next year counts as solved.
Read these shares as published figures, not as a measure of how well any agency performs.
:::

```{python}
fig, table = F.police_solved(rows)
chart_card(
    fig,
    title="Most offences against the human body were solved; about one in seven property offences were",
    subtitle=f"Share of police cases recorded as solved, by type of offence (%) · {FIRST} and {LAST}",
    alt=(
        f"Bar chart of the share of police cases solved. In {LAST}: against the human body "
        f"{pct(police(BODY, 'solved_pct'))}, various Acts {pct(police(VARIOUS, 'solved_pct'))}, "
        f"against property {pct(police(PROPERTY, 'solved_pct'))}, other Penal Code offences "
        f"{pct(police(PENAL, 'solved_pct'))}."
    ),
    provenance=prov_rows,
    table=table,
    height=380,
)
```

## Cases handled by other agencies, 2012–2013

A second table lists cases handled by other agencies under specific Acts:
`{python} num(other_first)` in `{python} FIRST` and `{python} num(other_last)` in
`{python} LAST`. Drug cases and customs and excise cases were the two largest groups,
together `{python} pct(drug_share_last + customs_share_last)` of the `{python} LAST` total. Almost all of these cases were recorded as solved, but the two tables count different
kinds of cases, so their solved shares shouldn't be compared.

Acts with fewer than 5 cases in either year are merged into "Other Acts" to protect privacy.
For the Labour Act, the source doesn't publish solved cases or arrests.

```{python}
fig, table = F.other_agency_cases(rows)
chart_card(
    fig,
    title=f"Drug cases rose from {num(other(DRUGS, 'cases', FIRST))} to {num(other(DRUGS, 'cases'))}; customs cases changed little",
    subtitle=f"Cases handled by other agencies, by Act · {FIRST} and {LAST}",
    alt=(
        f"Bar chart of cases handled by other agencies. Customs and excise: "
        f"{num(other(CUSTOMS, 'cases', FIRST))} then {num(other(CUSTOMS, 'cases'))}. Misuse of "
        f"drugs: {num(other(DRUGS, 'cases', FIRST))} then {num(other(DRUGS, 'cases'))}. "
        f"Immigration: {num(other(IMMIGRATION, 'cases', FIRST))} then "
        f"{num(other(IMMIGRATION, 'cases'))}. Labour: {num(other(LABOUR, 'cases', FIRST))} then "
        f"{num(other(LABOUR, 'cases'))}. Other Acts are small."
    ),
    provenance=prov_rows,
    table=table,
    height=420,
)
```

## What changed from 2012 to 2013

Police cases rose `{python} rise(cases_change)`, from `{python} num(cases_first)` to
`{python} num(cases_last)`. Offences against property account for
`{python} num(prop_extra)` of the `{python} num(police_extra)` extra cases
(`{python} signed(change("police", PROPERTY))`). Offences against the human body changed little
(`{python} signed(change("police", BODY))`). Among other agencies, drug cases rose
`{python} rise(change("other agencies", DRUGS))`, while customs and excise cases changed
little (`{python} signed(change("other agencies", CUSTOMS))`).

With only two years, these are changes between two single years, not trends.

## Conclusion

- **What kinds of offences made up police cases, and how many were solved?** Offences against
  property: `{python} pct(prop_share_last)` of police cases in `{python} LAST`. About
  `{python} pct(solved_last)` of all police cases were recorded as solved in both years, from
  about `{python} pct(police(BODY, "solved_pct"))` of offences against the human body to
  `{python} pct(police(PROPERTY, "solved_pct"))` of property offences.
- **What changed from 2012 to 2013?** Police cases rose `{python} rise(cases_change)`, mostly
  from property offences. The mix of offences and the overall share solved stayed much the
  same. Among other agencies, drug cases rose the most in number.

::: {.callout-caution appearance="simple" title="What this doesn't tell us"}
<!-- Side note: required on every case study (DESIGN.md §4.1). -->
- **Crime today.** The latest published year is `{python} LAST`. Much may have changed since.
- **Trends.** Two years can't show a trend. A rise from one year to the next may not continue.
- **All crime.** These are cases recorded by the police and other agencies. Offences that
  weren't reported or detected aren't counted, and more cases can mean more reporting or
  enforcement as well as more offences.
- **Detail.** There are no districts, months or specific offences (such as theft or assault)
  inside the four police groups, and no population figures to turn counts into rates.
- **Missing values.** Some cells are "-" in the source, which isn't explained. They are
  treated as missing, so solved counts for the Labour Act and "Other Acts" are incomplete.
:::
